s.t: A little tailor sat in his small shop.
s.fr: Un petit tailleur était assis dans sa petite boutique.

s.t: He sewed at his table.
s.fr: Il cousait à sa table.

s.t: One morning, he spread jam on fresh bread.
s.fr: Un matin, il étala de la confiture sur du pain frais.

s.t: Flies smelled the jam.
s.fr: Des mouches sentirent la confiture.

s.t: Seven flies flew to his bread.
s.fr: Sept mouches volèrent vers son pain.

s.t: The tailor grabbed a big cloth from the corner.
s.fr: Le tailleur attrapa un grand tissu dans le coin.

paras.summary: A little tailor sews in his small shop, and one morning he spreads jam on fresh bread; the smell draws flies, and seven fly to his bread, so he grabs a big cloth from the corner.

s.t: He hit the flies hard.
s.fr: Il frappa les mouches fort.

s.t: Seven flies fell down dead.
s.fr: Sept mouches tombèrent mortes.

s.t: The tailor saw seven dead flies on the table.
s.fr: Le tailleur vit sept mouches mortes sur la table.

s.t: "Seven at one blow!" said the tailor.
s.fr: « Sept d’un seul coup ! » dit-il.

s.t: He smiled at what he had done.
s.fr: Il sourit de ce qu’il avait fait.

s.t: No one else saw it.
s.fr: Personne d’autre ne le vit.

s.t: The tailor wanted the world to know.
s.fr: Le tailleur voulait que le monde sache.

paras.summary: He hits the flies hard and kills seven at once, then sees the dead flies and declares, "Seven at one blow!" smiling at what he has done; though no one else saw it, the tailor wanted the world to know.

s.t: The tailor sewed a belt from cloth.
s.fr: Le tailleur cousit une ceinture dans du tissu.

s.t: He sewed words on the belt.
s.fr: Il cousit des mots sur la ceinture.

s.t: The words said, "Seven at one blow."
s.fr: Les mots disaient : « Sept d’un seul coup. »

s.t: The little tailor put on his belt.
s.fr: Le petit tailleur mit sa ceinture.

paras.summary: The tailor sews a belt from cloth and sews words on it that read, "Seven at one blow," then puts on his belt.

s.t: He walked out into the street.
s.fr: Il sortit dans la rue.

s.t: People in the street read the words on his belt.
s.fr: Les gens dans la rue lurent les mots sur sa ceinture.

s.t: People believed the tailor had killed seven men.
s.fr: Les gens crurent que le tailleur avait tué sept hommes.

s.t: No one knew the seven were only flies.
s.fr: Personne ne savait que les sept n’étaient que des mouches.

s.t: He wanted to see the big world.
s.fr: Il voulait voir le grand monde.

s.t: "I will see the world," the tailor said.
s.fr: « Je verrai le monde », dit-il le tailleur.

paras.summary: He walks out into the street, where people read the words and believe he has killed seven men, though the seven were only flies, and he wants to see the big world, saying he will see the world.

s.t: He took bread and cheese for the road.
s.fr: Il prit du pain et du fromage pour la route.

s.t: A bird came to him.
s.fr: Un oiseau vint à lui.

s.t: He grabbed the bird and put it in his coat.
s.fr: Il saisit l’oiseau et le mit dans son manteau.

s.t: The tailor walked out to see the world.
s.fr: Le tailleur sortit pour voir le monde.

paras.summary: He takes bread and cheese for the road; a bird comes to him, and he grabs it, puts it in his coat, and walks out to see the world.

s.t: The tailor walked into a big forest.
s.fr: Le tailleur entra dans une grande forêt.

s.t: A giant sat by the road.
s.fr: Un géant était assis au bord de la route.

s.t: The giant looked down at the little tailor.
s.fr: Le géant regarda en bas le petit tailleur.

s.t: "Who are you?" the giant asked.
s.fr: « Qui êtes-vous ? » demanda le géant.

paras.summary: The tailor walks into a big forest, where a giant sits by the road; the giant looks down at the little tailor and asks who he is.

s.t: The tailor showed the giant his belt.
s.fr: Le tailleur montra au géant sa ceinture.

s.t: The giant read the words on the belt.
s.fr: Le géant lut les mots sur la ceinture.

s.t: The giant believed the tailor had killed seven men.
s.fr: Le géant crut que le tailleur avait tué sept hommes.

s.t: "Show me you are strong," the giant said.
s.fr: « Montre-moi que tu es fort, » dit le géant.

paras.summary: The tailor shows the giant his belt, and the giant reads the words and believes he has killed seven men, so the giant challenges him to show his strength.

s.t: The giant picked up a stone and squeezed it hard.
s.fr: Le géant ramassa une pierre et la serra fort.

s.t: Water dripped from the stone.
s.fr: De l’eau gouttait de la pierre.

s.t: "You try," the giant said.
s.fr: « Essayez », dit le géant.

s.t: The tailor took a cheese from his coat.
s.fr: Le tailleur prit un fromage de son manteau.

s.t: He squeezed the cheese hard.
s.fr: Il serra le fromage fort.

s.t: Water ran from the cheese to the ground.
s.fr: De l’eau coula du fromage jusqu’au sol.

paras.summary: The giant picks up a stone and squeezes it hard until water drips out, then tells the tailor to try; the tailor takes a cheese from his coat, squeezes it hard, and water runs from the cheese to the ground.

chapterList.title: The Bird That Never Came Down

s.t: The giant picked up a big stone.
s.fr: Le géant ramassa une grande pierre.

s.t: He threw the stone into the trees.
s.fr: Il lança la pierre dans les arbres.

s.t: The stone flew and fell to the ground.
s.fr: La pierre vola et tomba au sol.

s.t: "Try again," the giant said.
s.fr: « Essayez encore », dit le géant.

paras.summary: The giant picks up a big stone and throws it into the trees; it flies and falls to the ground, and the giant tells the tailor to try again.

s.t: The tailor took a small bird from his coat.
s.fr: Le tailleur prit un petit oiseau de son manteau.

s.t: He threw the bird up.
s.fr: Il lança l’oiseau en l’air.

s.t: The bird flew away and did not come down.
s.fr: L’oiseau s’envola et ne revint pas.

s.t: The giant looked up at the empty trees.
s.fr: Le géant leva les yeux vers les arbres vides.

paras.summary: The tailor takes a small bird from his coat and throws it up, and the bird flies away and does not come down; the giant looks up at the empty trees.

s.t: He moved back from the little tailor.
s.fr: Il recula loin du petit tailleur.

s.t: The giant believed the tailor had killed seven men.
s.fr: Le géant croyait que le tailleur avait tué sept hommes.

s.t: He had another plan for the tailor.
s.fr: Il avait un autre plan pour le tailleur.

s.t: "Come to my cave for the night," the giant said.
s.fr: « Viens dans ma grotte pour la nuit, » dit le géant.

s.t: "I will come," said the tailor.
s.fr: « Je viendrai, » dit le tailleur.

paras.summary: The giant moves back from the little tailor, believing he has killed seven men, and makes another plan for him, telling the tailor to come to his cave for the night; the tailor agrees to come.

s.t: The giant took the tailor into the cave.
s.fr: Le géant emmena le tailleur dans la grotte.

s.t: Other giants sat by a fire.
s.fr: D’autres géants étaient assis près d’un feu.

s.t: The giants gave the tailor a bed.
s.fr: Les géants donnèrent au tailleur un lit.

s.t: But the bed was too big for the little tailor.
s.fr: Mais le lit était trop grand pour le petit tailleur.

paras.summary: The giant takes the tailor into the cave, where other giants sit by a fire; the giants give the tailor a bed, but it is too big for the little tailor.

s.t: He did not lie in the middle of the bed.
s.fr: Il ne se coucha pas au milieu du lit.

s.t: He slept in a corner.
s.fr: Il dormit dans un coin.

s.t: At night, a giant came to the bed.
s.fr: La nuit, un géant vint au lit.

s.t: He wanted to kill the tailor.
s.fr: Il voulait tuer le tailleur.

s.t: The giant held a big bar.
s.fr: Le géant tenait une grande barre.

paras.summary: He does not lie in the middle of the bed and sleeps in a corner instead; at night, a giant comes to the bed, wanting to kill the tailor, and holds a big bar.

s.t: He hit the middle of the bed hard.
s.fr: Il frappa fort le milieu du lit.

s.t: But the bed was empty.
s.fr: Mais le lit était vide.

s.t: In the morning, the tailor walked out of the cave.
s.fr: Le matin, le tailleur sortit de la grotte.

s.t: The other giants saw him alive.
s.fr: Les autres géants le virent vivant.

s.t: The giants believed no one could kill the tailor.
s.fr: Les géants croyaient que personne ne pouvait tuer le tailleur.

s.t: They ran away into the forest.
s.fr: Ils s’enfuirent dans la forêt.

paras.summary: He hits the middle of the bed hard, but the bed is empty; in the morning, the tailor walks out of the cave, and the other giants see him alive and believe no one could kill him, so they run away into the forest.

s.t: The little tailor walked to a big city.
s.fr: Le petit tailleur marcha vers une grande ville.

s.t: The king lived in the city.
s.fr: Le roi vivait dans la ville.

s.t: People told the king about the tailor.
s.fr: Les gens parlèrent au roi du tailleur.

s.t: They told him about the belt.
s.fr: Ils lui parlèrent de la ceinture.

paras.summary: The tailor walks to a big city, where the king lives among many people, and word of the tailor reaches the king, who hears about his belt.

s.t: The belt said, "Seven at one blow."
s.fr: La ceinture disait « Sept d’un seul coup ».

s.t: The king believed the tailor had killed seven men.
s.fr: Le roi croyait que le tailleur avait tué sept hommes.

s.t: "I want this tailor in my army," said the king.
s.fr: « Je veux ce tailleur dans mon armée », dit le roi.

s.t: The king sent for the tailor.
s.fr: Le roi envoya chercher le tailleur.

s.t: The tailor came to the king's castle.
s.fr: Le tailleur vint au château du roi.

paras.summary: The belt reads, "Seven at one blow," so the king believes the tailor has killed seven men and wants him in the army, sending for him; the tailor comes to the castle.

s.t: He showed the king his belt.
s.fr: Il montra au roi sa ceinture.

s.t: "You may join my army," the king said.
s.fr: « Vous pouvez rejoindre mon armée », dit le roi.

s.t: Strong soldiers saw the tailor at the castle.
s.fr: De forts soldats virent le tailleur au château.

s.t: They read his belt and were afraid.
s.fr: Ils lurent sa ceinture et eurent peur.

s.t: The soldiers did not want to fight him.
s.fr: Les soldats ne voulaient pas se battre contre lui.

paras.summary: He shows the king his belt, and the king says he may join the army, but soldiers who see him at the castle read the belt, are afraid, and do not want to fight him.

chapterList.title: A Plan to Get Rid of Him

s.t: The soldiers went to the king.
s.fr: Les soldats allèrent voir le roi.

s.t: "This tailor is too dangerous," they said.
s.fr: « Ce tailleur est trop dangereux », dirent-ils.

s.t: "He may kill one if he is angry," a soldier said.
s.fr: « Il peut tuer quelqu’un s’il est en colère », dit un soldat.

s.t: The king still needed his army, but not an angry tailor.
s.fr: Le roi avait encore besoin de son armée, mais pas d’un tailleur en colère.

paras.summary: The soldiers go to the king and say this tailor is too dangerous, since he may kill one of them if he is angry; the king still needs his army, but not an angry tailor.

s.t: The king thought and asked his men what to do.
s.fr: Le roi réfléchit et demanda à ses hommes quoi faire.

s.t: "Give him a very hard task," one man said.
s.fr: « Donnez-lui une tâche très difficile », dit un homme.

s.t: "Two giants live in a dark forest," the man said.
s.fr: « Deux géants vivent dans une forêt sombre », dit l’homme.

s.t: "They kill people in the kingdom," he said.
s.fr: « Ils tuent des gens dans le royaume », dit-il.

s.t: "Send the tailor to kill the two giants," the man said.
s.fr: « Envoyez le tailleur tuer les deux géants », dit l’homme.

paras.summary: The king asks his men what to do, and one man suggests giving the tailor a very hard task — killing two giants who live in a dark forest and kill people in the kingdom.

s.t: The king wanted this plan.
s.fr: Le roi voulait ce plan.

s.t: The king sent for the tailor again.
s.fr: Le roi fit appeler le tailleur de nouveau.

s.t: "Kill the two giants in the dark forest," the king said.
s.fr: « Tuez les deux géants dans la forêt sombre », dit le roi.

s.t: "If you do this, you may marry my daughter," the king said.
s.fr: « Si vous faites cela, vous pouvez épouser ma fille », dit le roi.

s.t: "You will have half my kingdom," the king said.
s.fr: « Tu auras la moitié de mon royaume, » dit le roi.

paras.summary: The king wants this plan and sends for the tailor again, telling him to kill the two giants in the dark forest; if he does this, he may marry the king's daughter and will have half the kingdom.

s.t: The tailor walked to the dark forest.
s.fr: Le tailleur marcha jusqu’à la forêt sombre.

s.t: He saw two giants by a big tree.
s.fr: Il vit deux géants près d’un grand arbre.

s.t: The two giants were still asleep.
s.fr: Les deux géants dormaient encore.

s.t: The tailor climbed the big tree.
s.fr: Le tailleur grimpa dans le grand arbre.

s.t: He sat on a branch.
s.fr: Il s’assit sur une branche.

paras.summary: The tailor walks to the dark forest, where he sees two giants asleep by a big tree; he climbs the tree and sits on a branch.

s.t: The tailor had stones with him.
s.fr: Le tailleur avait des pierres avec lui.

s.t: He wanted to trick the two giants.
s.fr: Il voulait tromper les deux géants.

s.t: If the giants fought, they could kill each other.
s.fr: Si les géants se battaient, ils pourraient se tuer l’un l’autre.

s.t: The tailor picked up a stone.
s.fr: Le tailleur ramassa une pierre.

paras.summary: The tailor has stones with him and wants to trick the two giants, thinking that if they fought, they could kill each other, so he picks up a stone.

s.t: He threw the stone at the first giant.
s.fr: Il lança la pierre sur le premier géant.

s.t: The stone hit the first giant hard.
s.fr: La pierre frappa le premier géant avec force.

s.t: The first giant was angry.
s.fr: Le premier géant était en colère.

s.t: "You hit me!" the first giant said.
s.fr: « Tu m’as frappé ! » dit le premier géant.

s.t: "I did not hit you," the second giant said.
s.fr: « Je ne t’ai pas frappé, » dit le deuxième géant.

paras.summary: He throws the stone at the first giant, and it hits him hard; the first giant is angry and says, "You hit me!" but the second giant says he did not hit him.

s.t: It was morning now.
s.fr: C’était le matin maintenant.

s.t: "You hit me," the first giant said again.
s.fr: « Tu m’as frappé, » dit encore le premier géant.

s.t: The tailor dropped another stone from the tree.
s.fr: Le tailleur laissa tomber une autre pierre de l’arbre.

s.t: The stone hit the second giant.
s.fr: La pierre frappa le deuxième géant.

s.t: The second giant was very angry now.
s.fr: Le deuxième géant était très en colère maintenant.

paras.summary: It is morning now; the first giant insists the second hit him, and the tailor drops another stone from the tree, hitting the second giant, who grows very angry.

s.t: "You started this fight!" the second giant said to the first.
s.fr: « Tu as commencé cette bagarre ! » dit le deuxième géant au premier.

s.t: The two giants started to fight and hit each other hard.
s.fr: Les deux géants commencèrent à se battre et à se frapper fort.

s.t: They fought until they fell down dead.
s.fr: Ils se battirent jusqu’à ce qu’ils tombèrent morts.

s.t: No more giants lived in the forest.
s.fr: Plus aucun géant ne vivait dans la forêt.

s.t: The tailor climbed down from the tree.
s.fr: Le tailleur descendit de l’arbre.

paras.summary: The second giant accuses the first of starting the fight, and the two giants start to fight and hit each other hard until they fall down dead, and no more giants live in the forest.

s.t: He walked back to the king's castle.
s.fr: Il retourna au château du roi.

s.t: "How did you kill the giants?" the king asked.
s.fr: « Comment avez-vous tué les géants ? » demanda le roi.

s.t: "They killed each other," the tailor said.
s.fr: « Ils se sont tués l’un l’autre, » dit le tailleur.

s.t: The king was very surprised.
s.fr: Le roi fut très surpris.

s.t: The king wanted one more task done first.
s.fr: Le roi voulait d’abord une tâche de plus accomplie.

paras.summary: The tailor climbs down from the tree and walks back to the king's castle; he tells the king the giants killed each other, and the king, very surprised, wants one more task done before he pays the reward.

s.t: "Catch a unicorn in the forest," the king said.
s.fr: « Attrapez un licorne dans la forêt, » dit le roi.

s.t: The tailor went to the forest again.
s.fr: Le tailleur alla de nouveau dans la forêt.

s.t: He saw a unicorn.
s.fr: Il vit une licorne.

s.t: It had one long horn and white fur.
s.fr: Elle avait une longue corne et une fourrure blanche.

s.t: The unicorn put its head down to charge.
s.fr: La licorne baissa la tête pour charger.

paras.summary: The king tells the tailor to catch the unicorn in the forest, and the tailor goes there again; he sees a unicorn with one long horn and white fur, and it puts its head down to charge.

s.t: The unicorn ran at the tailor fast.
s.fr: La licorne courut vite vers le tailleur.

s.t: The tailor jumped behind a big tree.
s.fr: Le tailleur sauta derrière un grand arbre.

s.t: Its horn went into the tree.
s.fr: Sa corne entra dans l’arbre.

s.t: The horn was stuck in the tree trunk.
s.fr: La corne était coincée dans le tronc de l’arbre.

s.t: It was trapped and could not pull the horn out.
s.fr: Il était piégé et ne pouvait pas tirer la corne dehors.

paras.summary: The unicorn runs at the tailor fast, but he jumps behind a big tree, and its horn goes into the tree, stuck fast in the trunk, so it is trapped and cannot pull the horn out.

s.t: The tailor came out from behind the tree.
s.fr: Le tailleur sortit de derrière l’arbre.

s.t: He tied a rope around its neck.
s.fr: Il attacha une corde autour de son cou.

s.t: The tailor led it to the castle.
s.fr: Le tailleur le conduisit au château.

s.t: "This is the unicorn," the tailor said to the king.
s.fr: « Voici la licorne, » dit le tailleur au roi.

s.t: The king had never seen a unicorn.
s.fr: Le roi n’avait jamais vu de licorne.

paras.summary: The tailor comes out from behind the tree, ties a rope around its neck, and leads it to the castle; he tells the king, "This is the unicorn," and the king has never seen a unicorn.

s.t: "Catch a wild boar in the forest," the king said.
s.fr: « Attrapez un sanglier sauvage dans la forêt, » dit le roi.

s.t: The little tailor went into the forest.
s.fr: Le petit tailleur entra dans la forêt.

s.t: Soon he saw a small chapel with benches.
s.fr: Bientôt il vit une petite chapelle avec des bancs.

s.t: It had one small window.
s.fr: Elle avait une petite fenêtre.

paras.summary: The king tells the tailor to catch the wild boar in the forest, so he goes into the forest; he soon sees a small chapel with benches and one small window.

s.t: The wild boar ran out of the trees with two tusks.
s.fr: Le sanglier sortit des arbres avec ses deux défenses.

s.t: It charged at the tailor fast.
s.fr: Il chargea le tailleur rapidement.

s.t: He ran into the chapel, and the boar ran in too.
s.fr: Il courut dans la chapelle, et le sanglier y courut aussi.

s.t: The tailor jumped over a bench and out of the window.
s.fr: Le tailleur sauta par-dessus un banc et sortit par la fenêtre.

paras.summary: The wild boar runs out of the trees with two tusks and charges at the tailor fast; he runs into the chapel, with the boar running in too, and jumps over a bench and out of the window.

s.t: He ran around the chapel fast and shut the door.
s.fr: Il courut autour de la chapelle rapidement et ferma la porte.

s.t: The wild boar was now shut inside.
s.fr: Le sanglier était maintenant enfermé à l’intérieur.

s.t: The chapel bell rang.
s.fr: La cloche de la chapelle sonna.

s.t: The tailor walked back to the big castle.
s.fr: Le tailleur retourna au grand château.

s.t: "The boar is in the chapel," the tailor told the king.
s.fr: « Le sanglier est dans la chapelle », dit le tailleur au roi.

s.t: The king was surprised again.
s.fr: Le roi fut de nouveau surpris.

paras.summary: He runs around the chapel fast and shuts the door, trapping the wild boar inside as the chapel bell rings; the tailor walks back to the big castle and tells the king the boar is in the chapel, and the king is surprised again.

s.t: The tailor did the third task.
s.fr: Le tailleur accomplit la troisième tâche.

s.t: The king had no more tasks to give.
s.fr: Le roi n’avait plus de tâches à donner.

s.t: The king had given his word.
s.fr: Le roi avait donné sa parole.

s.t: "You may marry my daughter now," the king said.
s.fr: « Vous pouvez épouser ma fille maintenant, » dit le roi.

paras.summary: The tailor completes the third task, and the king, with no more tasks to give and having given his word, tells the tailor he may now marry his daughter.

s.t: Soon the tailor married the king's daughter.
s.fr: Bientôt le tailleur épousa la fille du roi.

s.t: All the people in the kingdom came to the wedding.
s.fr: Toutes les personnes du royaume vinrent au mariage.

s.t: Bells rang in the kingdom.
s.fr: Des cloches sonnèrent dans le royaume.

s.t: The king gave the tailor half the kingdom.
s.fr: Le roi donna au tailleur la moitié du royaume.

s.t: The tailor now had half the kingdom.
s.fr: Le tailleur avait maintenant la moitié du royaume.

paras.summary: Soon the tailor marries the king's daughter, and all the people in the kingdom come to the wedding as bells ring in the kingdom; the king gives him half the kingdom, which the tailor now has.

s.t: The tailor was now very rich.
s.fr: Le tailleur était maintenant très riche.

s.t: He never sewed again.
s.fr: Il ne recousit jamais plus.

s.t: The tailor was still strong and lived in the big castle.
s.fr: Le tailleur était encore fort et vivait dans le grand château.

s.t: People still said he was the little tailor with the belt.
s.fr: Les gens disaient encore qu’il était le petit tailleur avec la ceinture.

s.t: No one forgot "Seven at one blow."
s.fr: Personne n’oublia « Sept d’un seul coup ».

s.t: The tailor and the king's daughter danced all night.
s.fr: Le tailleur et la fille du roi dansèrent toute la nuit.

paras.summary: The tailor is now very rich and never sews again, though he is still strong and lives in the big castle, and people still say he is the little tailor with the belt, never forgetting "Seven at one blow"; the tailor and the king's daughter dance all night.

s.t: One night, the king's daughter heard the tailor in his sleep.
s.fr: Une nuit, la fille du roi entendit le tailleur dans son sommeil.

s.t: "Sew the coat, boy," the tailor said in his sleep.
s.fr: « Couds le manteau, garçon, » dit le tailleur dans son sommeil.

s.t: The king's daughter knew he was a tailor.
s.fr: La fille du roi savait qu’il était tailleur.

s.t: She did not want people to know.
s.fr: Elle ne voulait pas que les gens le sachent.

s.t: The king's daughter told the king.
s.fr: La fille du roi dit au roi.

paras.summary: One night, the king's daughter hears the tailor in his sleep, telling a boy to sew a coat, and she knows he is a tailor; not wanting people to know, she tells the king.

s.t: That night, the king's guards would take the tailor away.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, les gardes du roi emmèneraient le tailleur.

s.t: But one guard warned the tailor first.
s.fr: Mais un garde avertit le tailleur en premier.

s.t: That night, the tailor pretended to sleep.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, le tailleur fit semblant de dormir.

s.t: The guards came to his bed.
s.fr: Les gardes vinrent à son lit.

paras.summary: That night, the king's guards plan to take the tailor away, but one guard warns the tailor first, so the tailor pretends to sleep when the guards come to his bed.

s.t: "Seven at one blow!" the tailor said.
s.fr: « Sept d’un seul coup ! » dit le tailleur.

s.t: "I killed two giants and caught a unicorn," he said.
s.fr: « Je tuai deux géants et attrapai une licorne, » dit-il.

s.t: "I shut a wild boar in a chapel too," he said.
s.fr: « J’enfermai aussi un sanglier dans une chapelle, » dit-il.

s.t: The guards heard this and were afraid.
s.fr: Les gardes entendirent cela et eurent peur.

s.t: They ran away and did not come back.
s.fr: Ils s’enfuirent et ne revinrent pas.

s.t: The little tailor stayed happy.
s.fr: Le petit tailleur resta heureux.

paras.summary: The tailor says he killed seven at one blow, killed two giants, caught a unicorn, and shut a wild boar in a chapel too; the guards hear this, grow afraid, and run away and do not come back, and the little tailor stays happy.
